findings_and_open_questions.kind: newly assessed conditional contract question; no alias or unique count claimed
findings_and_open_questions.historical_relationship: 059 adler/READ-L11-377 and segovb/READ-L12-775 explicitly treated <=1e-12 kg pinning as an intentional numerical massless policy; do not relabel their finding or represent this as historical runtime evidence. REVIEW-L3-SHELL-TOPOLOGY-INDEX-AND-DENSITY-ADMISSION q3296 and L2-SHELL-TOPOLOGY-NATIVE-MASS-CLASSIFICATION q2449 remain related, with exact alias open.
findings_and_open_questions.condition_and_reasoning: Symbolic finite triangle with vertices (0,0,0), (2^-20,0,0), (0,2^-20,0), unit areal density, has nonzero edges and area 2^-41 square metres. The source vertex share is about 1.52e-13 kg per vertex, positive and finite. Source ShellMesh validation checks finite/nonnegative mass and permits it, but inverse_mass maps each <=1e-12 kg to zero PINNED. The source chain from mesh topology through Shell::new therefore represents a nondegenerate low-mass shell as prescribed motion.
findings_and_open_questions.limits: A symbolic static argument, no fixture, geometry or product run. This is an exceptionally small scale; supported minimum scale, error budget and product policy must be decided before calling it an ordinary garment defect. Zero-mass vertices intentionally pinned remain valid.
findings_and_open_questions.future_repair_acceptance: Establish a justified supported mass/geometry scale and make treatment of positive below-threshold mass explicit at the owning admission boundary, or retain mobility with stable arithmetic where supported. Later check true zero and finite positive masses near the boundary and representative mesh scales.

findings_and_open_questions.kind: newly assessed conditional derived-invariant question; alias unconfirmed
findings_and_open_questions.historical_relationship: Related to q445 SEGOVB-L12-CONNECTED-SURFACE-SOLVE-MASS-VALIDITY-ADMISSION and adler READ-L11-377 / segovb READ-L12-776 derived-overflow qualifications; not the same assertion failure or a proven exact alias.
findings_and_open_questions.condition_and_reasoning: Public SurfaceContacts::solve can receive finite ParticleInverseMass values; solve_inner asserts each is finite/nonnegative. A valid symbolic contact with vertex-to-triangle gradient weights [1,-1,0,0] can arise at a triangle corner. Two corresponding inverse masses f32::MAX each pass that validity check, while the f32 weighted-response sum overflows to +infinity. With finite positive depth 0.5 and unit gradients, the finite numerator divided by that infinite denominator yields signed zero in the f32 mathematical model and no position correction for those entries.
findings_and_open_questions.limits: Assumes that a suitable contact candidate is delivered and those masses/gradients reach that path. This is a source and arithmetic inference, not a constructed or executed scenario. ShellMesh inverse-mass conversion bounds canonical finite reciprocals by its massless threshold; ordinary producers, platform behavior and intended supported mass ranges remain open.
findings_and_open_questions.future_repair_acceptance: Define finite derived-response admission and stable scaling/normalization or explicit rejection before an infinite denominator can be classified active; later validate extreme finite inputs, zero/pinned contributions and ordinary contact behavior.

No ordinary Shell producer collision was found in bounded source; custom kernel namespace may intentionally permit overrides and needs a contract decision.
findings_and_open_questions.future_repair_acceptance: Define ownership/reservation of built-in solve bindings versus kernel-specific attachment names, validate collisions before retaining attachments, and preserve explicit custom-kernel capabilities. Later verify standard and intended custom bindings on both dispatch paths.

findings_and_open_questions.kind: recovered open concern, bounded canonical-producer qualification
findings_and_open_questions.historical_relationship: q625 and q1859 retain actual kernel stride and attachment-contract questions; q450 concerns structured error for the existing whole-multiple predicate and is not automatically the same defect.
findings_and_open_questions.condition_and_reasoning: For one constraint, attach_raw accepts any length as a multiple of one, including one word; the BEND shader indexes each constraint at eight-word stride and reads offsets 0–4. This generic API does not prove that a supplied record has the selected kernel schema. By contrast, Shell::new validates equal bend and bend-weight counts, reorders [f32;8] records, flattens and attaches them.
findings_and_open_questions.limits: No malformed buffer was created and no shader was run; bounds/native behavior is not asserted. The observed standard Shell producer does not demonstrate an ordinary wrong-width error. Kernel schema and whether raw custom attachments require external ownership remain open.
findings_and_open_questions.future_repair_acceptance: Carry each kernel attachment record layout and expected element stride to its admission and binding boundary, preserving valid empty constraints and custom formats; later verify required extent and per-record color permutation.

findings_and_open_questions.kind: recovered open concern, explicit public-input conditions
findings_and_open_questions.historical_relationship: q625 and q1859 already identify membership and short reorder as unresolved; no automatic new unique count.
findings_and_open_questions.condition_and_reasoning: ConstraintIncidence validates nonzero arity and complete records, while ParticleIndex explicitly does not prove membership in any particular particles buffer. ConstraintSet is built without a Particles argument and record_solve binds whichever one is supplied; the shader consumes the stored indices. Separately, public reorder indexes each value by the existing permutation and a nonempty set with an empty values slice would index out of bounds if called. distance and spring check matching array counts before their own reorder calls.
findings_and_open_questions.limits: No constructor, panic or shader has been executed. The mismatch is representable at public APIs, not proof a standard producer supplies it. Normal Shell validates index bounds and per-constraint data before building sets.
findings_and_open_questions.future_repair_acceptance: Bind constraint incidence to an admitted particle population or validate membership when pairing the set and particles, and check public permutation input shape with a structured error. Later verify cross-population mismatch and correct reordered paired data.

findings_and_open_questions.historical_relationship: 059 q176 and q452 SEGOVB-L12-CONNECTED-XPBD-SUBSTEP-ADMISSION are related historical observations; preserve identifiers and leave exact alias to central reconciliation.
findings_and_open_questions.condition_and_reasoning: record_step returns for nonpositive delta and zero substeps, but NaN is not <=0; direct record_substep accepts its substep without local validation. Constraint solve passes it to compliance/(h*h), and finalize divides position change by h. A merely finite positive representable h can also have an unrepresentable squared magnitude, so the arithmetic policy needs more than a sign check.
findings_and_open_questions.limits: No numerical division or GPU execution was performed; actual higher-level caller restrictions and device behavior remain open. Empty particles, zero substeps and disabled constraint sets are documented modes, not automatically defects.
findings_and_open_questions.future_repair_acceptance: Admit and carry a substep whose required reciprocal and square behavior satisfy the supported numeric contract before any batch mutation, while preserving intended no-op modes. Later verify direct and frame-derived boundaries.

findings_and_open_questions.historical_relationship: 059 q177 and q453 SEGOVB-L12-CONNECTED-XPBD-SPRING-DAMPING-CONSUMER describe related historical families; exact alias central.
findings_and_open_questions.condition_and_reasoning: The spring API retains per-spring four-float parameters and shader source labels z damping, but the actual shader body reads x, y and w and never reads z or a velocity input. Conditional on a supplied nonzero intended damping value, the source does not use that value in spring response.
findings_and_open_questions.limits: No shader execution, concrete nonzero producer, platform verification or dynamic outcome. Global solver drag is a separate policy and is not assumed equivalent to per-spring damping.
findings_and_open_questions.future_repair_acceptance: Choose and expose the intended per-spring damping contract and implement its own response without silently conflating general solver drag; later compare differing per-spring damping with other parameters fixed.

thirteen_lens_dispositions.producer_propagation: Partial: source traces density→triangle shares→mass→inverse mass→particle packing, incidence/color permutation→attachments→named shader binding, and CCD gradients→response. Other producers and native outcomes remain open.
thirteen_lens_dispositions.existing_type_owners: Partial: ParticleMass, ParticleInverseMass, ParticleArealDensity, ConstraintIndex/Count, ParticleIndex, effective response and gradient are distinct existing owners; a nominal wrapper does not itself establish validity or membership.
thirteen_lens_dispositions.admission_contracts: Partial: ShellMesh validates finite positions/masses and topology indices; ConstraintIncidence validates arity/complete records; generic raw-value and shared population/kernel-schema admissions remain open.
thirteen_lens_dispositions.invariant_operations: Partial: positive tiny mass conversion and finite f32 response overflow expose policy choices; substep square/reciprocal and count narrowing require bounded arithmetic contracts.
thirteen_lens_dispositions.aggregate_states: Partial: private coloring/arity coexist with public particle/lambda/attachment buffers, and incidence is not tied to a target Particles instance; no standard caller failure claimed.
thirteen_lens_dispositions.type_ownership: Partial: layout schema, typed mass and shader parameter identity have distinct owners; signed gradient and affine weight should not be forced into one bounded probability type.
thirteen_lens_dispositions.redundant_authority: Partial: stored color order, incidence and parallel buffers must retain a shared population and permutation; fixed and attachment binding names can contend. No whole-system single-authority verdict.
thirteen_lens_dispositions.behavior_preservation: Partial: assigned source bodies equal at both revisions; historical tiny-mass and zero-pinned policy intentionally preserved as evidence. Empty sets, zero substeps and disabled modes require explicit treatment.
thirteen_lens_dispositions.enum_shapes: Partial: validity, mobility and projection activity are purpose-specific enums; disabled set and absent work remain intentional, and no unsupported shape conversion asserted.
thirteen_lens_dispositions.derivability: Partial: wrappers, From, Sum and arithmetic implementations carry distinct semantics and bounds; no safe blanket derive replacement established.
thirteen_lens_dispositions.type_granularity: Partial: host count, native index, color slot, gradient, affine coefficient, mass and inverse mass are separate quantities; range or membership constraints should not be inferred merely from wrappers.
thirteen_lens_dispositions.magic_strings: Partial: attachment names are semantic GPU reflection keys, while set names and errors are diagnostics; the ability to shadow fixed binding keys is qualified, not a generic ban on raw text.
thirteen_lens_dispositions.magic_numbers: Partial: 1e-12 mass/contact/distance thresholds have distinct units and policy; only the tiny-positive-mass and overflow paths were reasoned through. No blanket threshold removal or whole-catalog clearance.

nonfindings_and_open_policy: Canonical Shell::new validates shell mesh and material before deriving particle masses or building stretch, seams and bending; current direct generic APIs have broader admitted input shapes.
True zero inverse mass is the intended prescribed-motion mode. Mass validity and mobility are separate: native float-word wrappers deliberately preserve values before explicit boundary checks.
Empty constraint sets and their unused one-word buffers, disabled sets, zero-substep no-op and intentional no-op hooks are supported modes; no backwards-compatibility inference.
Signed barycentric/gradient roles are affine/contact coefficients, not necessarily probabilities to be clamped into [0,1].
Compliance and spring payload validity, native capacity, actual allocation and actual custom callers remain open. No exact alias decision or global whole-lens clearance is made.
